catalog_quote: [Elugbe 1986: 51] Ghotuọ is a terraced level tone system with three basic tones and a downstep. We shall call these basic tones High (H), Mid (M), and Low (L). We shall refer to downstep with the abbreviation DS and symbolize it with an exclamation mark (!) before the downstepped syllable. Ghotuọ also has downdrift (DD): successive nonlows (i.e. H and M) are progressively lowered by the Ls that precede them. In Ghotuọ, unlike in Yala (Ikom) (the best known example of a language with three tones and a downstep), M does not have a downdrift effect on H. [Elugbe 1989: 88, sec.4.14.8 Tone] There is no doubt that Ghotuọ operates a three-level tone system and that the third level should be interpreted as 'mid'. There are no restrictions on the mid level in Ghotuọ. Elugbe (1973) makes a convincing case for this view of Ghotuọ tone.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ghotuo is described purely as a terraced-level tone language with three lexical/grammatical tones (High, Mid, Low) plus downstep and downdrift; none of the primary descriptions (Elugbe 1973, 1986, 1989a, 1989b; Adeniyi 2012; Bankale & Elugbe 2019) mentions word stress or accent at all, so no stress placement rule is stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal details: !H does not occur (only !M and !L per Elugbe 1986); Elugbe 1973: 235 had analysed 'three tonemes.. no downstep', revised by 1985/1986 to three tones plus downstep; Adeniyi 2012 reports speakers can suppress downstep depending on discourse factors.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern the lexical/grammatical tone system of the word and clause. Elugbe 1973: 237 notes that all prepausal non-low tones are realized as falling on verbs, some particles and pronouns, so monosyllabic verbs in citation form surface with a high-falling tone (a tonal, not accentual, citation-form effect).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Ghotuo (Ghotuọ, also Otuo/Otwa) = ghot1243 itself, North-Central Edoid, Owan/Akoko-Edo area of Edo State; no dialect differentiation is made. Elugbe's 1973 analysis (three tones, no downstep) was revised by Elugbe 1985/1986/1989 to three tones plus downstep; same language, same author.

sources.note: Ghotuo sketch sec.4.14 (pp.86-88): syllable structure, consonants, 7 oral vowels, no vowel harmony; sec.4.14.8 Tone p.88: three-level tone system, third level = mid, no restrictions on mid. General sec.3.5 Tone: Edoid systems range from three level tones (Ghotuo) to two levels +/- downstep. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the book (only 'heavily accented variety of Yoruba', sociolinguistic).
